newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices edge up on cool Texas temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices edge up on cool Texas temps.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices edged up Monday in lackluster trade, helped by cooler temperatures in Texas though most thought the rally would be short-lived with more moderate forecasts for midweek, sources said.

With little variation from seasonal weather expected for most of the nation this week and eastern utilities still trying to trim stocks, most agreed physical prices would be back on the defensive soon.
"The trend is your friend and the trend is lower. We don't see any bullish weather out there," said one trader, noting Gulf Coast swing prices were up slightly at $2.35-2.40 today.

Traders said the eastern stock surplus, now 153 bcf or 23 percent over last year, was likely to grow further after this week's AGA data, and with less than six weeks of winter left, trimming inventories was likely to remain a priority in the near term.

Prices in south Texas gained a couple of cents to the $2.30-35 level, still more than 40 cents below Feb 1 levels. With producing region stocks still more than 15 percent below year-ago, traders said prices there would remain vulnerable to cold weather spikes.
In west Texas, Permian prices were three cents higher in the high-$2.20s, still 30 cents below index.
Midcontinent prices held steady in the low-$2.30s, about 40 cents below Feb 1.
In the East, New York city-gate gas prices were steady to up a nickel to $2.90-95.
Swing prices at the southern California border were quoted almost five cents higher in the mid-to-high-$2.40s.
